title: Exposure Keratopathy: Pathophysiology to Management
summary: Exposure keratopathy represents a spectrum of corneal pathology resulting from incomplete eyelid closure (lagophthalmos), leading to ocular surface desiccation. It is a critical clinical challenge requiring prompt intervention to prevent secondary infection, ulceration, and vision loss.

sections.title: Red Flags: Urgent Intervention
content: Infiltrate or hypopyon (Rule out infectious keratitis)
Corneal thinning/melting (Impending perforation)
Severe conjunctival injection/pain
Decreased visual acuity (Progression beyond superficial punctate keratopathy)

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Protocol
content: Step 1: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy with Fluorescein staining to delineate epithelial defect.
Step 2: Measure lagophthalmos distance in mm using a ruler.
Step 3: Schirmer's test/TBUT to assess total tear film insufficiency.
Step 4: Corneal sensation testing (CN V integrity).
Step 5: If ulceration is present: Corneal scraping for culture and sensitivity.

content.explanation: A: Artificial tears (frequent), B: Barrier (lubricating ointment), C: Closure (taping/suture), D: Dew (humidity chamber), E: Eyelid surgery (tarsorrhaphy).

sections.title: Differential Diagnosis
content: Neurotrophic Keratitis (diminished corneal sensation)
Severe Dry Eye Disease (SS, MGD)
Infectious Keratitis (Bacterial, Fungal, Viral)
Traumatic Abrasions
Drug Toxicity (preservative-induced)

sections.title: Step-by-Step Management Ladder
content: Level 1: Preservative-free artificial tears Q1H and viscous gels QHS.
Level 2: Moisture chamber goggles or taping the eyelid closed at night.
Level 3: Therapeutic Scleral Contact Lens or Amniotic Membrane Transplantation.
Level 4: Temporary tarsorrhaphy (suture or adhesive).
Level 5: Surgical reconstruction (Gold weight, ectropion repair, or permanent tarsorrhaphy).

sections.title: Clinical Pearls
content: Always evaluate for concurrent Bell's Palsy or structural lid malposition.
Overnight protection is paramount; the blink reflex is absent during sleep.
If a patient is in an ICU setting, prophylactic lubrication is mandatory to prevent 'ICU-related exposure keratopathy'.
Corneal melting can occur rapidly; monitor thickness via anterior segment OCT if suspicion is high.
